mainEvent.title: Wed 11/25 · PCE inflation, Q3 GDP, durable goods and jobless claims all land at 8:30a
mainEvent.body: Thanksgiving squeezes the week's data into Wednesday morning. October core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, is expected to rise **0.3%** on the month and **3.2%** on the year, up from 3.1%, with headline PCE seen at 3.8% from 3.6% (AskTraders, FXEmpire, Newsquawk); Polymarket puts 3.2% at about 62% and 3.3% at 35%. The second estimate of Q3 GDP (advance **3.4%**), October durable goods and jobless claims, moved up a day, come out at the same time, then new home sales at 10:00a and the Fed's Beige Book at 2:00p. A December 9 hike is almost fully priced after last week's hawkish minutes, so a hot print could revive talk of a half-point move, while a soft one would back Treasury Secretary Bessent's Sunday warning against over-tightening. Before that: Dell, HP and Workday report Tuesday after the close. Markets are shut Thursday and close at 1:00p Friday.

regime.label: Risk-off
regime.text: Last week was the worst since April 2025: S&P 500 −8.6%, Nasdaq −10.0%, Dow −8.0%, Russell 2000 −7.5%. The S&P fell seven days straight and joined the Dow in a correction, the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026, and the chip index lost about 17%. Treasuries were the only haven that worked. Futures bounced Sunday evening.

stories.title: Futures bounce Sunday evening after the worst week since April 2025.
stories.body: S&P 500 futures were up **1.5%** at 7,036.50, Nasdaq 100 futures **2.4%** and Dow futures 0.9% at 6:23p Sunday, about 20 minutes after the reopen (Yahoo Finance futures data); FX Leaders and CNBC also reported futures opening higher. Last week the S&P 500 lost **8.6%** to 6,910.39, the Nasdaq **10.0%** to 22,617.73, the Dow 8.0% to 48,147.33 and the Russell 2000 7.5%, the worst week since April 2025 (FXEmpire, Palma Futures, Journalarta). The S&P fell seven sessions in a row, the longest streak since February 2020, and closed in a correction along with the Dow; the Nasdaq gave up its 2026 gain. The VIX closed at **35.89** Friday after touching 40, and CNN's Fear & Greed index sits at **9.7**, extreme fear, from 37 a week earlier. On CBS's Face the Nation, Treasury Secretary Bessent blamed "a combination of things": a selloff that "began as the Democrats moved ahead in the polls and then accelerated after Election Day", the Democratic position on the AI build-out, and "very hawkish remarks from the Federal Reserve" (CBS transcript). It is a short week: closed Thursday, 1:00p close Friday.

stories.title: Bessent warns the Fed against over-tightening before Wednesday's PCE.
stories.body: "Many people believe that they may be making a policy mistake if they over-tighten," Treasury Secretary Bessent said Sunday, pointing to "a substantial tightening in financial conditions over the past few months" (CBS Face the Nation transcript, investingLive). Markets still see a December 9 hike as close to certain: CME FedWatch had about **97%** on 25bp as of Friday (Yahoo Finance, BigGo), and Kalshi has a 25bp hike at **89%**, a hold at 8% and a bigger hike at 3%. The October minutes showed almost all officials saw more hikes as likely, Governor Cook warned Friday of getting "behind the curve" and Waller has argued for a half-point move. This week: NY Fed President Williams speaks Monday at 4:00p, core PCE is due Wednesday at 8:30a (est 3.2% y/y; Polymarket puts 0.3% m/m at about 92%), and the Beige Book follows at 2:00p. The pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday. Treasuries rallied hard last week: the 10Y fell **23bp** to 4.92% and the 2Y 25bp to 4.63% (Treasury).

stories.title: Nvidia: SEC inquiry, a delayed 10-Q and Bessent's call for answers.
stories.body: Nvidia fell **14%** to **$125.53** Friday, and about 23% on the week, after Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues; the SEC declined to comment and no wrongdoing has been found (Reuters via TipRanks, Journalarta). The WSJ first reported an SEC probe on Nov 17, and Nvidia has not yet filed its quarterly 10-Q; UBS said management linked the delay to the investigation and possible new risk disclosures (Reuters via Khaleej Times, TechCrunch via FourWeekMBA). FourWeekMBA puts the filing deadline at Dec 4. On Sunday Bessent said "we do need answers" from Nvidia's board, that the administration will "see if Megaspeed was indeed a pass-through company" for chips, and that Jensen Huang "is on the outside now" (CBS transcript); last week he gave the board 10 days, which ends about Nov 25 (Fox News via FourWeekMBA, Motley Fool). CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Polymarket gives about 15% that a permanent CEO is named by Dec 31 and 56% that the next CEO comes from outside.

stories.title: Earnings: Dell and HP test AI hardware demand; retailers report before Black Friday.
stories.body: Dell reports after Tuesday's close (call 4:30p). It guided fiscal Q3 to adjusted EPS of about **$6.50** on **$49.0B** of revenue, and the Street is at $6.48–6.62 (company guidance and Nasdaq via StockTitan, FXEmpire, TipRanks); Polymarket gives about 88% that it tops $6.71. HP Inc. (est about $0.74), Workday, Autodesk and Nutanix also report Tuesday evening, after Hewlett Packard Enterprise (est $1.17–1.29), Zoom and Agilent on Monday. Before Tuesday's open come Analog Devices (est about $3.89, revenue $4.32B), Medtronic, and a run of retailers into Black Friday: Best Buy (est about $1.48), Dick's ($1.38–1.42), Dollar Tree, Burlington, Abercrombie and Kohl's. Deere reports Wednesday before the open (est about $4.06). Trip.com moved its report to Dec 1 (StockTitan).

stories.title: Anthropic starts its first full week of trading barely above its $83 IPO price.
stories.body: Anthropic (**ANT**) closed at **$88.91** Friday, down 8.5% from its $97.17 debut close, after trading as low as $83.05, five cents above the $83 IPO price; volume fell to about 400 million shares from 857 million on day one (FinanceFeeds citing Nasdaq.com and Yahoo Finance; TipRanks). It opened at $111.50 on its first trade Thursday, so it is now about 20% below that print. Seaport Research started coverage at Neutral with no price target, citing slowing revenue growth (FinanceFeeds). The deal raised about $93.5B including selling holders, plus a $26B private placement at $83 with Microsoft, Google, Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom (TipRanks). Its fade from the opening print was one of the triggers of last week's AI selloff (AP, Reuters).

stories.title: Oil slips Sunday evening after a third weekly loss on a supply glut.
stories.body: WTI was at **$82.71**, down 1.5%, at 6:23p Sunday (Yahoo Finance futures data). January WTI settled at **$83.41** Friday, up $0.97, and Brent at **$92.57**, up $0.59 (Newsquawk, Bloomberg via Rigzone), but Brent lost 3.4% on the week, its third straight weekly drop, and WTI about 6% (Palma Futures). The IEA sees a supply surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter, and Energy Secretary Chris Wright said flows through the Strait of Hormuz are at a record (Bloomberg via Rigzone), even as tankers keep getting hit near Oman: UKMTO reported a tanker struck in its engine room about 6 miles north of Khasab on Nov 18, crew safe and no one blamed (Gulf News, Newsquawk). Gold fell about 9% last week to roughly $3,515–3,540 but was up 1.9% Sunday evening. OPEC+ meets Nov 29.
